analyst_view.overall: Hoffenheim (23rd, 4 pts) host Sturm Graz (24th, 4 pts) in a game both need to stay in the play-off race, with Christian Ilzer facing his old club. Hoffenheim are without defenders Valentin Gendrey (broken fibula) and Albian Hajdari, with Robin Hranac and Nathan De Cat also out for several more weeks; all four are on the numbers' list. Ozan Kabak's suspension is a Bundesliga one, so he should be available here, and Alexander Prass is back training after a complaint. Sturm Graz have no new absences beyond those listed (Grgic, Khudyakov, Kiteishvili, Rozga) but have lost three of their last four, including 2-3 at home to Celje in Europe. Portuguese referee Luis Godinho (about 4.5 cards a game) is in charge; with nothing the numbers cannot see, every stat stays where they put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (Hoffenheim 2.1) and already include Hoffenheim's recent form and the defensive absences on their list. Kabak should be available in Europe and Sturm have no new injuries, so nothing points either way and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, mostly Hoffenheim (7.1), already up a little for Sturm winning corners lately. Hoffenheim should have most of the ball at home, which the split shows, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already up about 10% for Hoffenheim drawing many bookings from opponents lately and about 5% for referee Luis Godinho (4.5 a game). Ilzer's reunion with his old club adds some edge but no sign of bad blood, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.1 shots, already up about 11% for Hoffenheim's busy recent shooting (103 in six). With no new absences in their attack, I stay at 32.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already a little lower for Sturm's recent finishing. Andrej Kramaric and the rest of Hoffenheim's attack are available, so I stay at 9.8.
